ground_truth_soap:
Subjective:
Chief Complaint (CC):
The patient presents for an initial consultation regarding his nicotine dependence.

History of Present Illness (HPI):
John Doe, a 38-year-old Caucasian male, has been smoking 15-20 cigarettes daily for the past 15 years. He reports very strong cravings, especially in the mornings, and has episodes of coughing, particularly in the morning. He mentions difficulty concentrating and increased irritability when not smoking.

Review of Systems (ROS):
- General: Reports sleep issues, getting 6-7 hours per night but often disrupted.
- ENT: Mild morning cough.
- Respiratory: No wheezing or shortness of breath noted.
- Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations.
- Gastrointestinal: No issues reported.
- Neurological: Difficulty concentrating, increased irritability when not smoking.
- Mental Health: Initially resistant to quitting but willing to try nicotine replacement therapy and see a counselor.

Objective:
Vital Signs:
- BP: 135/85 mmHg
- Pulse: 76 bpm
- Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
- Temperature: 98.4°F

Physical Exam:
- HEENT: Mild erythema of the oropharynx, no exudates.
- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs.
- Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezing.

Assessment:
- Nicotine Dependence, Cigarettes, Uncomplicated.
- Hypertension.
- Hyperlipidemia.

Plan:
Nicotine Dependence:
- Prescribed Nicotine replacement therapy: Nicotine patches, 21 mg, once daily for 6 weeks.
- Referral to smoking cessation counselor, Dr. Jane Smith, for behavioral therapy support.
- Follow up in 1 month to assess progress and make any necessary adjustments.

Hypertension and Hyperlipidemia:
- Await full lipid panel and subsequent blood pressure readings.
- Continue current antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications.

Instructions:
- The patient was advised to apply the nicotine patch daily in the morning.
- Schedule an appointment with Dr. Jane Smith for smoking cessation counseling.
- Maintain a blood pressure and diet log.
- Call the clinic with any concerns or adverse reactions to the nicotine patch.

The patient agreed to this plan and will follow up in 1 month.
